questions.prompt: SAMPLE — replace with authored content. Which statement best describes the sample concept?

options.text: The sample concept is the named idea this placeholder item is checking.
The sample concept is interchangeable with any nearby term.
The sample concept can be skipped when the wording feels familiar.
The sample concept is a label that never needs a contrast.

questions.rationale: SAMPLE — replace with authored content. The correct choice restates the sample concept without collapsing it into a neighboring idea.

questions.prompt: SAMPLE — replace with authored content. Why does the sample concept need an explicit contrast?

options.text: A contrast keeps the sample concept from being confused with a neighboring idea.
A contrast is optional once the sample concept has a name.
The sample concept collapses into whichever nearby term is more popular.
The sample concept can be skipped if the contrast is already obvious.

questions.rationale: SAMPLE — replace with authored content. The sample concept stays usable only when its contrast is named.

questions.prompt: SAMPLE — replace with authored content. How should a learner apply the sample concept in this second objective?

options.text: Restate the sample concept, then check it against the situation before choosing.
Skip the sample concept and choose the first familiar term.
Treat the sample concept as a label with no work behind it.
Drop the contrast and let neighboring ideas stand in.

questions.prompt: SAMPLE — replace with authored content. How does the sample concept connect across the two placeholder objectives?
